guards: a Go HTTP change with SQL built from a query parameter, a mutex left locked on an early return and a response body closed before the error check is reviewed as Go code
amended: Copied from ../cases/go-http-handler.json on 2026-10-08 to score this run with the scorer that needs words on every plant: each plant and side issue that had no mentions got them; no other field changed.

anchor.text: fmt.Sprintf("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE name = '%s'", name)

bugs.truth: The name from the query string is formatted into the SQL text, so a caller can run any SQL. The fix is a placeholder, QueryContext(ctx, "... WHERE name = ?", name).

Count takes the lock and returns early for a missing key without unlocking, so the next request to Count waits forever. The fix is defer h.mu.Unlock() right after Lock, or checking the key before taking the lock.
resp.Body.Close is deferred before err is checked; when http.Get fails, resp is nil and the deferred call panics. The fix is to check err first and defer the close after.

extras.why: http.Get uses the default client with no timeout, so a slow upstream holds the request forever; real, not planted
